docs.title: Learning Technology Tools Portal
docs.text: Welcome to the Learning Technology Tools Portal — a central hub for documentation on the tools our team builds and maintains.

docs.title: What's here
docs.text: Tool Description Learning Design Extension Browser extension and utilities for LXD workflows in Canvas ueu-canvas package Python package for interacting with the Unity Canvas LMS API Sprint Summary Script Trello reporting tool for generating sprint summaries LISA Instructor Insights & Compliance Dashboard

docs.title: How to navigate
docs.text:
Sidebar — Use the left navigation panel to browse documentation by tool. Click any section heading to expand it.

Search — Press the search icon (or S / /) to search across all documentation. Results update as you type and show which tool each result belongs to.

In-page navigation — Headings within a page appear in the right-side table of contents, letting you jump directly to a section.

docs.title: Getting help
docs.text: If something in the documentation is unclear or out of date, contact the Learning Technology team.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Follow instructions in https://github.com/Unity-Environmental-University/lxd-tools-build or README.dist.md, pointing the extensions loader to dist/

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This guide will walk you through setting up your local development environment for the LXD extension. Follow the steps below to create your local branches, install dependencies, build local changes, and test your work.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Git: Ensure you have Git installed and configured.
  • Node.js & npm: Verify that your Node.js and npm installations are up-to-date.
  • Existing Tools:
  • lxd-tools repository
  • GitHub Desktop(optional): Depending on your familiarity working with Git in the command line, GitHub Desktop may be a helpful tool for pulling repos and committing your code changes.

docs.title: 1. Create a Local Branch of lxd-tools
docs.text:
1. Clone the lxd-tools repository:

git clone <URL_TO_LXD_TOOLS_REPOSITORY>

cd lxd-tools

  1. Install dependencies:

npm install

Note: These dependencies are also defined in the package.json of lxd-tools.

docs.title: 2. Starting Development
docs.text:
1. At this point, you should test if you're able to build the extension locally. In the lxd-tools directory, run npm run build. If that fails, you will need to address any errors.

  2. If your build is successful, you are ready to start working on code. Work can be done either in the current release branch(for small changes), your own testing branch, or a feature branch(if the work you're doing will go on to be it's own feature.) Make sure you checkout/create a branch that isn't main before you begin working.

  3. After you made changes, please document them in the Unreleased section of the change log

docs.title: 3. Testing Your Changes
docs.text:
1. Once the local build is working and you're in a non-main branch, you can make changes to the code and test them in the browser. To have a build of the extension that updates every time the code is changed, you can run npm run watch.

  2. Jest is the testing suite used for unit testing. Any time you change code, you should run the tests to make sure they still pass. Tests can be run with the command npm test.

docs.title: 4. Finalizing Your Changes
docs.text:
• Features that have passed testing and are ready to go into the extension can be pushed to the current release branch.
  • Features that still need work may be best placed in their own feature branch.

docs.title: Publishing the Extension
docs.text: This guide explains how to publish the LXD Extension.

docs.title: 1. Prepare Your Branches
docs.text:
• Merge Changes Down: Ensure that finished code in feature or development branches are merged down into the release branch.
  • Push Commits: Before starting the publishing process, verify that all users' finished changes on the release branch have been pushed to the remote repository.

docs.title: 2. Update the Version Number
docs.text:
• Increment the Version in package.json:

  • Open package.json and update the version field to the next release version (e.g., from 2.9.1.2 to 2.9.1.3).

  • Versioning in incremented based on the following:

    +0.0.0.1 for a hotfix +0.0.1 for sprint-based releases +0.1 for feature releases +1.0 for massive changes

docs.title: 3. Run Tests
docs.text:
• Test the Code: Run the test suite to validate that all tests pass successfully: npm test

  • Fix Any Failures: If any tests fail, resolve the issues before proceeding.

docs.title: 4. Build Locally and Test Manually
docs.text:
• Build the extension locally for testing

Run npm run build to build the extension locally

  • Test the Local Build Version: Perform a manual test of the extension in its intended environment. Verify that all functionalities work as expected.

docs.title: 5. Publish the Extension
docs.text:
• Execute the Publishing Command: Once you've built the extension, publish the extension by running the publish script: npm run publish

The publish script performs the following tasks:

  • Checks the current version from package.json and creates the corresponding package tag.
  • Ensures that the tag does not already exist in the distribution folder’s Git history.
  • Updates Git tags.
  • Reads the manifest (manifest.source.json) and synchronizes its version with the package version.
  • Stages changes, constructs a commit message from the differences between tags, commits the changes, and finally pushes commit and tags to the remote repository.

docs.title: 6. Communicate & Finalize the Release
docs.text:
• Notify the Team: Let everyone know about the new release. The people that use the extension are in The Mighty LXD Team chat on Microsoft Teams. Let them know there's a new version of the extension, including a few top level details about what is new.

  • Merge Current Release Branch into main in LXD-Tools Merge the current release branch into main in the lxd-tools repository.

  • New Release Branch in LXD-Tools: Create a new release branch in lxd-tools based on the newly merged main branch.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
1. Merge Changes Down:
  2. Consolidate updates from various branches into the release branch.
  3. Increment the Version:
  4. Update the version number in package.json.
  5. Run Tests:
  6. Run npm test Ensure all tests pass (fix any failing tests).
  7. Build Locally
  8. Run npm run build to build the extension locally for testing.
  9. Manual Testing:
  10. Manually verify that the extension works as intended.
  11. Build & Publish:
  12. Run npm run publish to publish the extension.
  13. Notify the Team:
  14. Communicate the new release to the team.
  15. Manage Release Branches:
  16. Merge changes in lxd-tools to main.
  17. Create a new release branch in lxd-tools for the new version.

docs.title: LXD Chrome Extension
docs.text:
This extension is for use by Unity Environmental University Learning Experience Designers working in Canvas.

Source repository: https://github.com/Unity-Environmental-University/lxd-tools

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
For most people who use this extension at Unity, it should now automatically install on your laptop. If it doesn't, you can follow the steps below:

  1. Clone this repository
  2. If you have GitHub Desktop installed, select Code → Open with GitHub Desktop
  3. Otherwise, select Code → Download ZIP, then extract the zip and place the folder somewhere easy to find
  4. Load the extension into Chrome:
  5. Go to chrome://extensions
  6. Enable Developer Mode (toggle in the top-right corner)
  7. Click Load unpacked and select the folder where you placed the extension files

Full walkthrough: https://webkul.com/blog/how-to-install-the-unpacked-extension-in-chrome/

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
1. If you are using GitHub Desktop, pull the latest version of this repository
  2. If you downloaded a ZIP:
  3. Download a fresh ZIP and extract it
  4. Replace all files in your original installation folder with the new ones, keeping the same filenames
  5. Go to chrome://extensions and click the Update button at the top of the page

GitHub Desktop download: https://desktop.github.com/

docs.title: Extension Popup
docs.text:
Click the extension icon in your browser toolbar (or press Alt+Shift+F) to open the popup panel. From here you can:

  • Search for courses by course code and jump directly to them in Canvas
  • Filter by subaccount (Distance Education, Distance Education Development, Unity College)
  • Open Salesforce reports with one click:
  • Undergrad Section Check
  • Grad Section Check
  • Unique Course Offerings by Term
  • Save your OpenAI API key (used by AI-powered features in the extension — see Advanced Options)

docs.title: Course Navigation Buttons
docs.text:
When viewing any Canvas course, the extension adds buttons to the top of the page:

Button What it does DEV Opens the DEV_ version of this course in a new tab BP Opens the Blueprint version of this course in a new tab BPs Shows a list of all available Blueprint versions of this course SECTIONS Opens all student sections linked to this Blueprint

These buttons try to take you to the same page you are currently on (e.g., the same assignment or discussion) in the corresponding course version. If a matching page is not found, the course home page opens instead.

docs.title: Quick Course Search (Keyboard Shortcut)
docs.text:
Press Alt+Shift+F to open a quick-search dialog. You can type:

Query Result DEV_TEST000 Navigate directly to that course w2a Open all assignments in Week 2 w2q Open all quizzes in Week 2 w2d Open all discussions in Week 2 w3d2 Go to the second discussion in Week 3 w1d0 Go to the course Introduction (usually Week 1, Discussion 0) DEV_TEST000\|w3q1 Go to the first quiz in Week 3 of a different course

docs.title: Links Button
docs.text: On any Canvas content page (pages, assignments, discussions), a Links button appears in the header. Clicking it opens all external links and file links embedded in that page in new tabs at once — useful for quickly checking that all resources in a lesson are accessible.

docs.title: Modules Page
docs.text:
When viewing the Modules page of a course, the extension adds two buttons to the header:

  • Lock All (Blueprint courses only) — Locks every module item in the Blueprint with a single click. The page reloads automatically when done.
  • Adjust Due Dates — Prompts you for a number of days, then shifts all assignment due dates in the course by that amount. Useful when copying a course to a new term.

docs.title: Rubric Reordering
docs.text:
When editing a rubric, the extension adds reordering controls to each rubric criterion row:

  • ↑ / ↓ buttons to move a criterion up or down
  • Drag and drop rows to reorder them directly (the dragged row turns semi-transparent, and a blue border shows the drop target)

The reorder controls appear when you enter edit mode and disappear when you save or cancel.

docs.title: SpeedGrader — Rubric Score Exports
docs.text:
On the Canvas SpeedGrader page, the extension adds export buttons to the gradebook header:

Button What it exports Rubrics: Assignment Rubric scores for the current assignment → Rubric Scores {AssignmentName}.csv Rubrics: Section Rubric scores for all assignments in the course → Rubric Scores {CourseCode}.csv ... (three dots) Opens a date-range picker to export scores for a specific term window → {CourseCode}-{StartDate}-{EndDate}.csv

A loading indicator appears while the export is being generated.

docs.title: Syllabus — Import Week 1 Materials
docs.text:
On the Course Syllabus page, an Import Wk1 Mats button appears above the "Week 1 Learning Materials" section. Clicking it:

  1. Reads the course's "Week 1 Learning Materials" page
  2. Extracts all video embeds and learning material boxes from that page
  3. Replaces the existing syllabus content in that section with the imported materials
  4. Resizes embedded video iframes to fit the syllabus layout

The page reloads automatically after a successful import.

docs.title: Large Image Warning
docs.text: When editing a Canvas page that contains a banner image wider than 2000px, the extension displays a prominent warning around the image. A Try Resize button appears — clicking it attempts to resize the image to 1200px wide.

docs.title: Home Tile Image Generator
docs.text:
On a course's Module Home section, a Generate Home Tiles button appears. This tool automatically creates marketing thumbnail images for the course:

  • Use Course Image checkbox — uses the course's banner image as the source (checked by default)
  • Module Number field — specify a module number as the image source (use 0 for the course-level image)
  • Click Generate to produce two image files:
  • {CourseCode}DetailImage.png (1920px wide)
  • {CourseCode}ListImage.png (600px wide)
  • A Salesforce Image Download button is also available to extract and download course images in Salesforce-compatible formats

docs.title: Version Update Notice
docs.text:
If a newer version of the extension is available, a banner appears on Canvas course pages alerting you:

You are not running the latest version (X.X.X) of the extension. You are running Y.Y.Y.

Follow the Updating steps above to get the latest version.

docs.title: Admin Panel
docs.text:
On course Settings and publishing pages, an Admin button opens a modal with tools for bulk operations across multiple courses:

  • Search courses by code or name, with filters for Blueprints, Legacy BPs, Dev copies, and Sections
  • Select and run validations to check course content against defined standards
  • View results showing which courses passed or failed, with direct links to each course
  • Sync Blueprint — trigger a Blueprint sync from the server for any Blueprint course

docs.title: Faculty Reporting
docs.text:
On Canvas account/admin pages, a Reporting button opens a modal where you can:

  • Select one or more terms
  • Find all instructors active in those terms
  • View a list of courses for those terms

docs.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
docs.text: Shortcut Action Alt+Shift+F Open the extension popup / quick course search

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This document describes the automated build and deployment process for the LXD browser extension. The workflow is triggered when a pull request is merged to the main branch and handles building, signing, and distributing the extension across multiple platforms (Chrome and Firefox).

The deployment pipeline manages version control, package signing, storage on Cloudflare R2, and maintains a clean version history.

docs.title: When the workflow runs
docs.text:
• A pull request is merged to the main branch
  • The event type must be 'closed' (not open, reopened, or synchronize)

docs.title: What triggers it NOT to run
docs.text:
• Pull request is closed without merging
  • Pull request is opened or updated

docs.title: Repository requirements
docs.text:
• Version number in package.json is updated with each release
  • Extension source code follows the npm build pipeline
  • updates.json and update.xml files are present in the dist directory

docs.title: Secrets and credentials
docs.text: Secret Name Purpose CHROME_KEY_PEM_B64 Base64-encoded Chrome extension signing key (PEM format) WEB_EXT_API_KEY Firefox AMO API key for signing WEB_EXT_API_SECRET Firefox AMO API secret for signing R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID Cloudflare R2 access key ID for storage R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY Cloudflare R2 secret access key CF_ACCOUNT_ID Cloudflare account ID for R2 endpoint R2_BUCKET_NAME Name of the Cloudflare R2 bucket for storage LXD_TOOLS_BUILD_TOKEN GitHub personal access token for lxd-tools-build repository

docs.title: Build Process Steps
docs.text:
The workflow performs the following automated steps in sequence:

  1. Repository Checkout & Setup — Clones the lxd-tools repository and installs Node.js 20 with all dependencies. Git tags are fetched to enable version detection.
  2. Version Validation — Reads the version from package.json and verifies it hasn't been deployed before by checking for an existing git tag. If a duplicate version is detected, the entire build fails with a clear error message to prevent accidental re-deployment.
  3. Extension Compilation — Runs npm run build to compile the extension source code into the dist directory.
  4. Platform-Specific Signing — The compiled extension is signed for both platforms:
  5. Chrome: Uses the crx3 tool with the private key to produce lxd-extension-{VERSION}.crx

  6. Firefox: Uses the web-ext sign command with AMO API credentials to produce lxd-extension-{VERSION}.xpi signed for the unlisted channel

  7. Artifact Verification — Validates that all required output files exist: both signed extensions (.crx and .xpi), plus the update manifests (updates.json and update.xml). File paths are captured for downstream steps.

  8. Upload to Cloudflare R2 — All artifacts are uploaded to the R2 bucket with appropriate content types. This includes both signed extensions and update manifests needed by the browser extension update mechanisms.
  9. Version Pruning — Automatically deletes old versions from R2, keeping only the 5 most recent releases of each file type (.crx and .xpi). This reduces storage costs while maintaining version history.
  10. Sync to Build Repository — The entire dist directory is copied to the lxd-tools-build repository on the main branch, creating an audit trail of all deployments with commits attributed to github-actions[bot].
  11. Git Release Management — A git tag matching the version number is created and pushed, and a corresponding release branch (release/{VERSION}) is created for long-term reference and potential rollback scenarios.

docs.title: Version Management
docs.text:
• package.json version must be incremented BEFORE merging the PR
  • The pull reqest will be blocked from merging unless the package version is bumped
  • Duplicate version deployments are prevented by version validation step
  • If version already exists, entire build fails with clear error message

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• All secrets are referenced via ${{ secrets.VAR_NAME }} syntax, per GitHub Actions format
  • Chrome key is base64-encoded and must be decoded before use
  • Firefox API credentials are environment variables, never logged
  • GitHub token used for pushing to build repository is scoped and temporary

docs.title: Storage Retention
docs.text:
• Only the 5 most recent versions are retained in R2
  • Older versions are automatically pruned to control costs
  • This applies to both .xpi and .crx files

docs.title: Repository Structure
docs.text:
• Source code: lxd-tools repository (main branch)
  • Built artifacts: lxd-tools-build repository (main branch)
  • This separation allows history tracking and rollback capability

docs.title: Workflow Execution Environment
docs.text:
• Runner: ubuntu-latest
  • Permissions: contents: write (for creating tags and commits)
  • Duration: Typically 5-10 minutes depending on npm install time

docs.title: File Outputs
docs.text:
After successful execution, the following files are available:

File Location Platform Purpose lxd-extension-{VERSION}.crx R2 bucket & dist/ Chrome Signed extension package lxd-extension-{VERSION}.xpi R2 bucket & dist/ Firefox Signed extension package update.xml R2 bucket & dist/ Chrome Update manifest for Chrome updates.json R2 bucket & dist/ Firefox Update manifest for Firefox

docs.title: Build fails at version validation
docs.text:
Cause: package.json version was not incremented

Solution:

  1. Update package.json with a new version number
  2. Push the change to a new commit or amend the PR
  3. Re-merge the PR to trigger the workflow again

docs.title: Chrome extension fails to sign
docs.text:
Cause: Invalid or missing CHROME_KEY_PEM_B64 secret

Solution:

  1. Verify the secret is properly base64-encoded
  2. Check that the PEM file is valid (openssl x509 -in cert.pem -text -noout)
  3. Update the secret in GitHub repository settings if needed
  4. Re-run the workflow

docs.title: Monitoring and Notifications
docs.text:
The workflow produces the following artifacts for monitoring:

  • GitHub Actions logs: Real-time build output in Actions tab
  • Git tags: Version tags created on successful deployment (visible in Releases)
  • Release branches: Version-specific branches created at release/{VERSION}
  • lxd-tools-build commits: Automatic commits showing deployment history

docs.title: Before modifying the workflow
docs.text:
1. Test changes in a separate branch
  2. Ensure all secrets are still available
  3. Verify npm build script still works
  4. Test signing keys are still valid
  5. Review and test any version management changes

docs.title: Knowledge Base
docs.text: The purpose of this is to collect extension-specific information as an attempt to make it easier to pick up developing the extension.

docs.title: Canvas Authentication
docs.text:
The extension does not use a standalone API Key. Instead, it piggybacks on the user’s active browser session. It authorizes requests by extracting the Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) token that Canvas already generated for the user.

Where we get it:

Primary: A hidden input field in the Canvas DOM: input[name='authenticity_token'].

Fallback: The browser cookie named \_csrf_token(which the extension manually decodes).

NOTE: If the university updates Canvas and they change the name of that input field or the cookie, all POST/PUT requests will fail (403 Forbidden).

docs.title: 'Style Guide'
docs.text: This is a set of general patterns in the codebase.

docs.title: Async/Await
docs.text: For the sake of code that runs asynchronously, await is used predominantly over .then()

docs.title: Intentionally unused variables
docs.text: The code was getting a lot of unused variable warnings that were false flags as those variables were being used outside of the file. Anywhere that happens, the variable now has a leading underscore to indicate that it is intentionally unused.

docs.title: Link checking
docs.text:
There are three patterns used in this codebase for checking URLs, depending on context:

1. Regex over raw HTML strings (syllabus/discussion content)

When checking whether a specific URL exists in an HTML string (e.g. a syllabus or discussion body), use new RegExp(escapedUrl, "ig") where escapedUrl has been sanitized with .replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&"). This escapes special regex characters in the URL so dots and other metacharacters are treated as literals. See makeSyllabusUrlCheck in syllabusTests.ts.

2. Quote-bounded substring check (HTML attribute values)

When checking for the presence or absence of a URL as an href value inside an HTML string, wrap the URL in double quotes: htmlString.includes("${url}"). Since HTML attributes are quoted, this ensures the URL is matched as an exact attribute value rather than as a substring of a longer URL (e.g. a redirect parameter). See aiPolicyMediaRun in syllabusTests.ts and the run function in discussionTests.ts.

3. URL hostname check (actual browser URLs)

When checking whether the current page URL belongs to a trusted host, parse the URI with new URL() and check the hostname property: new URL(document.documentURI).hostname.endsWith(".instructure.com"). Never use .includes() on a raw URL string to check the host — a URL like https://evil.com/?r=https://unity.instructure.com would falsely pass. See content/index.ts.

docs.title: GitHub Actions
docs.text: There are currently two active GitHub Action Workflows:

docs.title: Push Test
docs.text: On every commit, this action runs runs test coverage, linting and typechecking on the code to ensure that changes haven't caused any errors.

docs.title: PR Build
docs.text: On every pull request, this workflow will lint, typecheck and test the code and then create a build artifact that it will comment in the pull request, this makes it easier for a user to pull the built extension and test.

docs.title: Tips/Tricks
docs.text:
• npm run build:dev will build the extension at ../lxd-extension-build to create a local build. This was created so you could keep the released version along side a local version for testing
  • A Canvas test environment exists at https://unity.test.instructure.com/.
  • I find myself using a test course in the live Canvas more often, which allows me to reset and pull any course in.

docs.title: ueu-canvas
docs.text:
This is the source code for the @ueu/ueu-canvas npm package — a TypeScript library for interacting with the Canvas LMS API. It provides typed interfaces, data fetching utilities, and helpers for working with Canvas objects such as courses, enrollments, content items, terms, users, rubrics, and files.

The package is built with Webpack and TypeScript and publishes its compiled output from the dist/ directory.

docs.title: What's in here
docs.text:
• Courses — fetch course data, manage blueprint courses, modules, sections, and course start dates
  • Content — typed wrappers for Canvas content items: assignments, discussions, pages, and quizzes
  • Enrollments — enrollment generators and role helpers
  • Terms — term fetching and date parsing from term names
  • Users — user generators
  • Fetch — low-level utilities for paginated Canvas API requests (getPagedDataGenerator, fetchJson, typed GET/write configs)
  • Rubrics — rubric and rubric association types and helpers
  • Files — Canvas file types
  • Mocks — mock data for testing

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: npm install @ueu/ueu-canvas

docs.title: Build
docs.text: npm run build

docs.title: Test
docs.text: npx jest

docs.title: Tag a release to get auto-publish to run
docs.text:
git tag v1.1.1

git push origin v1.1.1

docs.title: Trello Reporting Tool
docs.text: A utility to create a draft Markdown file for reporting out on sprints. The tool pulls lists from a Trello board, asks the user to select which lists they want to use, then pulls the cards from those lists. It then creates a template Markdown file, as well as a csv of cards in matching lists and a Markdown file with some basic data analysis on the cards. After writing the public-facing report, the user can pull that out of the file to send off.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Environment: Create a .env file based on .env.example.
  2. Installation: Run pip install -r requirements.txt.
  3. Configuration: Ensure TRELLO_BOARD_ID is set to the right board.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Run python main.py.
  2. Select the lists you wish to review.
  3. Find the generated files in their specific folders
  4. /reports for the template file
  5. /csv for the card csv file
  6. /data for the data analysis file
  7. Use the resources to draft a sprint summary.

docs.title: File Structure
docs.text:
• main.py: Core logic and API integration.
  • /reports/: Local storage for generated template Markdown files (Git ignored).
  • /csv/: Local storage for generated csv files (Git ignored).
  • /data/: Local storage for generated data analysis files (Git ignored).
  • .env: API credentials (Git ignored).
  • .env.example: A file with required environment variable names to be filled in.
  • requirements.txt: Info for python requirements to be installed.

docs.title: LISA — Instructor Compliance Dashboard
docs.text: LISA is an "Instructor Insights"-style dashboard that allows deans to identify which instructors are behind on grading at a glance.

docs.title: Root-level files
docs.text: • shared_config.json — single source of truth for constants used by both the frontend and backend (page size, default sort columns/directions). Both lisa_backend/utils/constants.py and lisa_frontend/src/constants.ts read from this file.

docs.title: Backend (lisa_backend)
docs.text:
Written in Python using Flask. Serves a REST API backed by a PostgreSQL database running in Docker.

Database & Canvas data

The database is created and maintained using the instructure-dap-client Python package, which pulls data from Canvas's Data Access Platform (DAP) into PostgreSQL. See this repo for the Docker configuration.

Note: The Canvas DAP client requires linux-based Python. The backend must run inside WSL, a VM, or natively on Linux. Python 3.11+ is required; Python 3.12 is currently used.

Key files

  • services/compliance_service.py — query logic
  • api_server.py — Flask routes and server startup
  • SQLAlchemy reflects Canvas-managed tables automatically; app-owned tables are defined as explicit models in models/models.py and managed by Alembic.

Authentication

The ldap3 package handles authentication against Unity's Microsoft Active Directory. Only members of a specific AD group can log in using their campus credentials. Users must be on the Unity intranet to access LISA.

WSGI

Waitress is used as the production WSGI server (port 5000).

docs.title: Frontend (lisa_frontend)
docs.text:
Written in TypeScript using React and Vite. Standard React/Vite app — see lisa_frontend/ for source.

In production, the frontend is built (npm run build) and the resulting dist/ folder is served by Flask/Waitress alongside the API.

docs.title: Production Server (unitycanvas-tcc)
docs.text:
Remote access to this machine is controlled by IT.

Web server — IIS

Microsoft IIS acts as a reverse proxy, handling inbound traffic and forwarding it to Waitress: - Application Request Routing (ARR) and URL Rewrite modules are installed to enable reverse proxy. - Reverse proxy is enabled in ARR settings. - URL Rewrite rules redirect HTTP to HTTPS and forward all traffic to the Waitress process on port 5000. - Bindings: HTTP on port 80, HTTPS on port 443. - SSL certificates were provisioned by IT. - Subdomains https://lisa and https://lisa.campus.unity.edu provided by IT

WSL

The backend runs inside WSL due to the Linux Python dependency. Ubuntu 22.04 is currently used.

To install pg_isready (used by the sync script):

apt install postgresql

Scheduled sync

A cron job syncs the database twice daily via lisa_backend/scripts/run_sync.sh. Run lisa_backend/scripts/setup_sync_cron.sh to register it.

Database backups

lisa_backend/scripts/backup_db.sh dumps the database via the Docker container to /mnt/e/lisa_backups/ and prunes files older than 30 days. Run lisa_backend/scripts/setup_backup_cron.sh to register a daily midnight cron job for it.

Startup automation

Windows Task Scheduler is configured to automatically start Docker and run lisa_backend/scripts/launch_prod.sh inside WSL on machine startup.

docs.title: LISA Backend
docs.text: Flask API server for the LISA Instructor Compliance Dashboard. Pulls Canvas LMS data via the Instructure DAP client, stores it in PostgreSQL, and serves compliance metrics to the frontend.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.12 (required by scripts; 3.11+ is the minimum per DAP client docs)
  • Linux environment — the instructure-dap-client package requires linux-based Python. On Windows, run inside WSL.
  • PostgreSQL running and accessible (see Docker setup repo linked in the root README)
  • Node.js / npm — only needed if running the full dev stack via launch_dev.sh

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Create and populate .env

Copy env.example to .env and fill in all values. See Environment Variables below.

2. Install dependencies

uv sync

3. Initialize the database

The PostgreSQL database must already exist and be running. To populate it with Canvas data for the first time:

source .venv/bin/activate
python3.12 operate_db.py init all

This pulls all tracked tables from Canvas DAP into the database. It may take a while on first run.

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
From the repo root, scripts/launch_dev.sh starts both the Flask backend (port 5001) and the Vite frontend dev server in one step:

bash lisa_backend/scripts/launch_dev.sh

The frontend dev server proxies /api requests to the Flask process, keeping session cookies on the same origin. Note: the backend does not auto-reload on file changes (use_reloader=False) — restart it manually after edits.

To run just the backend:

export FLASK_ENV=development
uv run python3.12 api_server.py

docs.title: Production
docs.text:
scripts/launch_prod.sh starts the Waitress WSGI server on port 5000 and automatically restarts it on non-zero exits:

bash lisa_backend/scripts/launch_prod.sh

In production, Flask also serves the compiled frontend from ../lisa_frontend/dist/. Build the frontend before starting the server:

cd ../lisa_frontend && npm run build

On unitycanvas-tcc, this script is launched automatically at startup via Windows Task Scheduler.

docs.title: Database Sync
docs.text:
Canvas data is kept current by syncing with the DAP API. The sync script waits for PostgreSQL to be ready before running:

bash lisa_backend/scripts/run_sync.sh

This calls python3.12 operate_db.py sync all under the hood. On the production server, a cron job runs this script twice daily.

You can also trigger a sync at any time from the UI, or invoke operate_db.py directly:

# Sync all tables
python3.12 operate_db.py sync all

# Sync specific tables
python3.12 operate_db.py sync submissions,assignments

# Initialize (first-time load) specific tables
python3.12 operate_db.py init enrollments,courses

Tracked tables: users, courses, enrollment_terms, assignments, submissions, enrollments, content_tags, context_modules, discussion_entries, discussion_topics

docs.title: Database Indexes
docs.text:
The following partial indexes exist on the canvas schema to support compliance queries. They are partial (i.e. indexed over a filtered subset of rows) because every query that joins on these tables always includes the filter condition — inactive/deleted rows are never needed. Partial indexes are smaller and faster than full indexes on the same columns since PostgreSQL only indexes the rows that queries actually touch.

submissions - idx_submissions_course_user_active — btree on (course_id, user_id) where workflow_state NOT IN ('unsubmitted', 'deleted')

enrollments - idx_enrollments_course_user_active — btree on (course_id, user_id) where workflow_state = 'active' - idx_enrollments_teacher_active — btree on (user_id, course_id) where workflow_state = 'active' AND type = 'TeacherEnrollment'

courses - idx_courses_term_id — btree on (enrollment_term_id)

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Copy env.example to .env. All variables below are required for production.

Variable Description DAP_CLIENT_ID Instructure DAP API client ID DAP_CLIENT_SECRET Instructure DAP API client secret DAP_API_URL Instructure DAP API endpoint URL LISA_CANVAS_DB_NAME PostgreSQL database name LISA_CANVAS_DB_USER PostgreSQL username LISA_CANVAS_DB_PASSWORD PostgreSQL password LISA_CANVAS_DB_HOST PostgreSQL host (typically localhost) LISA_CANVAS_DB_PORT PostgreSQL port FLASK_ENV development or production FLASK_SECRET_KEY Secret key for Flask session encryption LDAP_SERVER LDAP server URL (e.g. ldaps://subdomain.domain.com) LDAP_BASE_DN Base DN for LDAP user searches LDAP_REQUIRED_GROUP Full CN of the AD group required for access

Security note: In production (FLASK_ENV=production), SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE is set to True, ensuring session cookies are only sent over HTTPS.

docs.title: API Endpoints
docs.text:
All endpoints are prefixed with /api. All except health and login require an active session.

Method Endpoint Description GET /api/health Server health and version info POST /api/login Authenticate with campus LDAP credentials POST /api/logout Clear session GET /api/me Current logged-in username GET /api/terms All available terms (id → name) GET /api/current_term Current term ID (?isUnderGrad=true/false) GET /api/dashboard/instructors Paginated grading compliance data per instructor GET /api/dashboard/discussion-instructors Paginated discussion response compliance data per instructor GET /api/dashboard/announcement-instructors Paginated announcement compliance data per instructor GET /api/courses/<id>/submissions Submissions for a specific course GET /api/discussions/<id>/responses Discussion responses for a specific discussion POST /api/sync_request Trigger a Canvas DAP sync (async, returns 202) GET /api/last_sync Timestamp of last successful sync GET /api/violations List all flags, optionally filtered by flag_term_id, flag_type, instructor_id POST /api/violations Create a new flag (instructor_id, flag_type, flag_term_id required; reason_for_flag optional) GET /api/violations/<id> Get a single flag by ID PUT /api/violations/<id> Update flag type and/or reason DELETE /api/violations/<id> Delete a flag GET /api/violations/counts Per-instructor flag counts for a given term (flag_term_id required)

Instructor/discussion/announcement endpoint query params: page, page_size, term, name, sort_column, sort_direction, start_date, end_date, is_CE

Submissions endpoint query params: page, page_size, sort_column, sort_direction, start_date, end_date

Violations list query params: flag_term_id, flag_type, instructor_id

docs.title: Compliance Logic
docs.text:
The core metric calculation lives in services/compliance_service.py. The key concept:

  • A submission is overdue if it has been sitting ungraded past the compliance window.
  • The window is 72 hours for standard courses and 48 hours for CE courses.
  • The window starts from the due date for on-time student submissions, or from the submission timestamp for late student submissions.

These thresholds are applied in get_compliance_for_courses(), which returns per-course counts that api_server.py aggregates per instructor.

The thresholds, excluded assignment titles, term name patterns, and course code regex patterns are all defined as named constants in utils/constants.py. Pagination defaults and default sort columns/directions are sourced from shared_config.json (repo root) via utils/constants.py.

docs.title: Key Dependencies
docs.text:
Package Purpose flask Web framework waitress Production WSGI server sqlalchemy ORM and database reflection psycopg2-binary PostgreSQL adapter instructure-dap-client Canvas DAP data sync ldap3 LDAP/Active Directory authentication python-dotenv .env file loading flask-cors CORS headers (development only)

To add or update dependencies, edit pyproject.toml then run:

uv sync

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
uv run pytest

Tests live in tests/test_compliance_service.py and use an in-memory SQLite database — no credentials or running PostgreSQL required.

What's covered:

  • get_term_info — correct id→name mapping, empty table
  • get_current_term — UG vs grad selection (DE5W/DE8W), excludes "test" terms, excludes expired terms
  • get_term_start_end — correct date lookup, nonexistent term
  • get_submissions_to_courses — workflow state filtering (unsubmitted/deleted excluded), excluded assignment titles (Introductions, Integrity 1 & 2), CE vs non-CE due date requirement, start/end date filtering, inactive enrollment exclusion, course ID scoping
  • get_compliance_for_courses — on-time overdue, late overdue, graded not counted as overdue, within-window not counted, 48h vs 72h threshold, multi-course grouping, CE mode column differences, date range propagation
  • craft_instructors_courses_query — query construction (execution requires PostgreSQL due to array_agg and regex ~ operator)

docs.title: Linting & Formatting
docs.text:
Ruff is our linter & formatter of choice. 

uv run ruff check
uv run ruff format

docs.title: LISA Frontend
docs.text: React + TypeScript frontend for the LISA Instructor Compliance Dashboard. Built with Vite.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
npm install

Copy ../.env.example or set VITE_API_BASE in a .env file:

VITE_API_BASE=http://localhost:5001/api

In development, Vite proxies /api requests to the Flask backend so session cookies stay on the same origin. In production, Flask serves the compiled dist/ directly and no proxy is needed.

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
# Development (Vite dev server on port 5173)
npm run dev

# Production build (output to dist/)
npm run build

Both the backend and frontend dev servers can be started together from the repo root with lisa_backend/scripts/launch_dev.sh.

docs.title: Views
docs.text:
The dashboard has four views, toggled by tab buttons at the top:

Grading Compliance — lists instructors with counts of overdue ungraded submissions. Clicking a row expands per-course detail; clicking a course opens the full submissions table for that course.

Discussion Response Compliance — lists instructors with their discussion response rates. Response rates are calculated per-discussion topic. Clicking a row expands per-course detail; clicking a course opens the discussion responses table.

Announcements — lists instructors with total announcement counts and scheduled announcement counts per course.

Flags — lists all recorded instructor flags (violations). Each row shows flag type (grading, discussions, announcements, other), term, date, and optional reason note. Flags can be edited or deleted inline. Filterable by term, instructor ID, flag type, reason text, and date range.

The three compliance views each include a flag column showing the instructor's current-term flag count and total lifetime flag count. Clicking the flag button opens a dialog to record a new flag. Grading, Discussion, and Announcements views share the same filter controls: instructor name search, date range, term selector, and CE toggle.

Instructor names are rendered as mailto links. Email addresses are derived from the instructor's name (first initial + last name + @unity.edu) because the canvas database does not store email addresses.

Links are set to open in new tab by default (<base target="_blank" />) in index.html

docs.title: State
docs.text:
All shared state (current term, filters, pagination, instructor lists, view toggle) lives in App.tsx. Components receive data and callbacks as props. The Go button triggers a fresh fetch; Prev/Next paginate the current result. A page indicator ("Page X of Y") is displayed in the main view alongside the pagination controls.

Syncing state is polled every 10 seconds after a manual sync is triggered, and the instructor data is automatically refreshed when the sync completes.
